voiceover:
[conversational] Every AI chat you've hit Share on is a link anyone can open.

In July, shared Claude chats showed up in Google. Stay till the end, because unsharing isn't the last thing to clean up.

[serious] The check takes 30 seconds. In Claude on the web: Settings, Privacy, then Manage next to Shared chats. Hit the trash icon on each one. Then do the same for Shared artifacts. It's a separate list.

In ChatGPT: Settings, Data controls, Manage next to Shared links. Then More actions, Delete all shared links.

[whispers] Honest catch: that kills the link, but not a copy someone already saved.

Now the part people miss. Deleting a chat doesn't delete what the AI remembered from it. So switch off memory too. Claude: Settings, Your Claude. ChatGPT: Settings, Personalization, Memory.

[curious] When did you last check your shared links? Send this to the friend who pastes work stuff into AI. Hack saved?

open_loop.setup: Stay till the end, because unsharing isn't the last thing to clean up.
open_loop.payoff: Deleting a chat doesn't delete what the AI remembered from it.

topic: Your AI chats can end up in Google search if you share them. Show how to check your shared links, delete them, and turn off the settings that expose your chats and artifacts.

pick.topic: Your AI chats can end up in Google search if you share them. Show how to check your shared links, delete them, and turn off the settings that expose your chats and artifacts.
pick.tool: Claude and ChatGPT sharing and privacy settings (shared links, published artifacts, memory)
pick.angle: Your AI chats aren't as private as you think. One 'Share' click can put them on Google. Check yours in 30 seconds.
pick.why: 190,851 views and 761 comments in 43s. Privacy warnings pull strong engagement, and the fix is a quick settings walkthrough. It's different from our Incognito and Memory reels because it covers shared links and published content. Frame it accurately: shared or public links and published artifacts can be indexed, not every chat.

research.tool: Claude: Settings > Privacy > Shared chats / Shared artifacts, plus Memory. ChatGPT: Settings > Data controls > Shared links, plus Personalization > Memory.
research.availability: Free on all consumer plans, on web and mobile apps. Claude's Share and Manage flow is documented for desktop web. ChatGPT Business and Enterprise differ: Business links open only to workspace members, and only Enterprise can disable sharing workspace-wide.
steps: CLAUDE (web, claude.ai): click your profile/name at the bottom-left, then click Settings.
Open the Privacy tab. Under the data section (labelled 'Your data' in recent guides, 'Data controls' in older Anthropic help text), find the 'Shared chats' row and click Manage.
A 'Shared chats' pop-up lists each chat's title, date shared and link. Click the Unshare (trash can) icon next to each one to kill the link. An empty list says 'No shared content found'.
Same page: click Manage next to 'Shared artifacts' and unpublish or unshare anything listed. This is a separate list from shared chats.
Alternative for one chat: open the shared chat, click Share (top right), and under 'Chat shared' choose 'Keep private'.

CLAUDE MEMORY: Settings > Your Claude (older layout: Settings > Memory). Turn off the memory toggle ('Memory from chats', called 'Generate memory from chats' in the older layout). Click Manage next to 'Your memory' to delete individual topics. Choose Pause (keeps what is saved) or Reset (deletes everything).
CLAUDE, one chat only: before sending the first message, click '+' and switch Memory off, or use an Incognito (ghost icon) chat.
CHATGPT (web): click your profile avatar at the bottom-left, then Settings, then Data controls. Next to 'Shared links' click Manage.
In that list, delete one link ('Delete shared link', or the trash/three-dot menu), or open 'More actions' and choose 'Delete all shared links'.

CHATGPT MEMORY: Settings > Personalization > Memory. Turn Memory off, or turn off 'Reference saved memories' and 'Reference chat history'. Use Manage or Saved memories to delete entries, or '•••' > 'Delete and turn off memory' to wipe and disable in one step. Labels vary by account.
facts: <cite index="8-2">Anthropic: chats are always private by default; you create snapshots to share via direct link.</cite>
<cite index="8-8,8-9">Anyone with the link can view the chat snapshot, which includes all messages before sharing, including artifacts.</cite>
<cite index="8-10,8-11">Messages sent after sharing stay private. If you unshare and share again, the snapshot updates with the new messages.</cite>
<cite index="2-11">Android Authority: review shared links at Settings > Privacy > Shared Chats and select Manage, where active links can be disabled.</cite>
<cite index="3-13">PCWorld: under Privacy you can click 'Shared chats' or 'Shared artifacts' to see what you've shared and make it private again.</cite>
<cite index="13-16">Shared artifacts have their own row and Manage button under Settings > Privacy, so revoking a chat doesn't revoke an artifact you published from it.</cite>

July 2026 incident: <cite index="4-2">Reddit members found that a specific Google search phrase pulled up a long list of shared Claude conversations.</cite> <cite index="5-4">The query was site:claude.ai/share.</cite>
<cite index="4-4,4-5">The links are no longer reachable through that technique. Claude conversations are private by default, and only chats users had shared were affected.</cite>

<cite index="1-6,1-7">Anthropic says chats become public only when a user creates a share link. It says it doesn't give search engines shared-chat directories, so the likely route is public pages that link to them, such as forums.</cite>
<cite index="2-8">Google points owners to a noindex tag to keep pages out of Search.</cite>
<cite index="5-8">Hackread: removing a page from Google Search does not delete the Claude conversation or disable its sharing link.</cite>
<cite index="4-6">Fortune: it's not the first time Claude chats have reached public Google searches.</cite>
Artifacts: <cite index="30-5,30-6">Anthropic says artifacts start private to you and nothing is shared until you share it.</cite>
<cite index="30-10,30-11,30-12">For newer shared artifacts, everyone needs a Claude account, even with the link. The exception is a legacy artifact published from a chat.</cite>
<cite index="30-15">Anyone with the link can view and use a published chat artifact without a Claude account.</cite>
<cite index="30-19">Anthropic: you can't publish an artifact again after you unpublish it.</cite>

<cite index="36-9,36-10">Pagelive (third-party): legacy artifacts, made in a chat before September 16, 2026, can be published on Free, Pro and Max. As of October 2026 the Publish button appears only on legacy artifacts.</cite>
<cite index="28-17">Codecademy: deleting a chat in Claude also unpublishes its associated artifacts.</cite>
Claude memory: <cite index="44-14">it's on by default for Free, Pro and Max and off by default on Team and Enterprise.</cite>

<cite index="38-1,38-7">Anthropic's help page gives the path as Settings > Your Claude (older layout: Settings > Memory). 'Generate memory from chats' is the toggle, and Manage next to 'Your memory' shows what Claude remembers.</cite>

<cite index="41-16,41-17,41-18,41-19,41-20">Pause keeps what Claude already knows but stops new additions. Reset permanently deletes everything, including project memories, and can't be undone.</cite>
<cite index="45-4">Chats are deleted within 30 days, but memories saved from them stay until you delete them in Settings > Memory.</cite>
ChatGPT shared links: <cite index="19-12">URL format is https://chatgpt.com/share/<conversation-ID>.</cite>
<cite index="19-16,19-17,19-18">OpenAI: view and manage all shared links from Settings > Data Controls. Find 'Shared links', click Manage, then delete individual links or all of them.</cite>
<cite index="23-9">Bulk delete is under 'More actions' > 'Delete all shared links'.</cite>
<cite index="19-8">OpenAI: shared links have no granular permissions.</cite>
<cite index="19-4">If someone replies to a conversation shared with them, a copy lands in their own history and is not deleted when you delete the shared link.</cite>

ChatGPT 2025 indexing episode: <cite index="9-3,9-4">per OpenAI's FAQ, chats appeared in search only if you manually enabled indexing, via a small 'Make this chat discoverable' checkbox in the share pop-up.</cite>
<cite index="27-13">A recent guide says ChatGPT used to have a checkbox that made a shared chat discoverable in search.</cite> That implies it has been removed.
<cite index="23-4">Changing 'Improve the model for everyone' does not delete existing shared links or change who can open them.</cite>
<cite index="47-10,47-13">OpenAI: turn memory off at Settings > Personalization > Memory. View and delete specific memories, or clear all, via Manage Memory.</cite>
<cite index="54-5,54-6">Turning off 'Reference saved memories' also turns off 'Reference chat history'.</cite>
<cite index="51-7">Turning ChatGPT memory off does not delete past chats.</cite> <cite index="47-7">Temporary Chat doesn't use or update memory.</cite>
do_not_claim: Do NOT say 'everything you share in Claude shows up in Google' or that 'anyone can Google your Claude chats today'. Only chats you explicitly shared via link were ever affected, and the site:claude.ai/share trick no longer works. Sources: Fortune, Yahoo/TechCrunch, Android Authority.
Do NOT say private or unshared chats were exposed. Every outlet says they were not.

Do NOT say Anthropic published or sent chats to Google. Anthropic says it gives search engines no directories. Likely path: someone posted the links publicly. Google says it doesn't control what pages are made public.
Do NOT claim 'bank statements, medical conditions and personal rants' were found. No source verifies those categories. Fortune lists erotica, programming chats, work notes and fake book reviews.
Do NOT say memory is public or Google-searchable. Memory is a personalization feature, not a public link. Frame it as 'what Claude remembers about you', not exposure.

Do NOT say Google will keep showing your chat after you unshare. Say instead that unsharing kills the link, but a copy someone already saved, or a cached snippet, isn't covered. Only 'does not remove a copy someone already saved' is directly sourced (managednerds). No source states cache behaviour.

Do NOT say 'ChatGPT still has a Make this chat discoverable checkbox'. It was reported in 2025 and appears to have been removed. Only a secondary source confirms the removal, so avoid stating it as current UI.
Do NOT say deleting a chat always deletes its ChatGPT share link. Sources conflict: Bitdefender says no, Jazz.security says yes. Tell viewers to delete the link in Shared links itself.
Do NOT say you can unpublish and republish an artifact. Unpublish is permanent for that artifact.
Do NOT use the older label 'Shared links' for Claude. Current guides say 'Shared chats' and 'Shared artifacts'. 'Shared links' is the ChatGPT label.

Do NOT say you can only check this on desktop. Privacy International (older, about 13 months) says mobile can view but only the browser can delete. That is unverified for today, so say 'use the web version'.
criticism: Anthropic describes shared chats as public snapshots, and some reporting says shared pages lacked a noindex directive. <cite index="6-4">MatrixTribe (secondary): Anthropic describes shared chats as publicly accessible snapshots, while reporting found some shared pages lacked a noindex directive.</cite>
<cite index="5-9">Hackread: many users take 'anyone with the link' to mean only people who receive the URL, not search results.</cite>
<cite index="4-7">Fortune: shared chats are typically more sensitive than a shared document, because people think out loud about work, health and legal problems.</cite>
<cite index="33-14">ShareDuo (third-party): Claude does not serve a noindex header on published artifact pages (legacy claude.ai/public/...).</cite> Treat this as unverified by Anthropic.
<cite index="33-19">ShareDuo (third-party): published artifact links stay live until you manually unpublish them, with no expiry option.</cite>
<cite index="19-8,19-9">ChatGPT shared links have no granular permissions, and the FAQ points to deleting links as the only way to end access.</cite>
Deleting a chat does not remove the memory entries made from it, on either Claude or ChatGPT. Anthropic's help page puts the normal deletion window at 30 days.

Anthropic keeps some data after deletion. Per whizi.io's reading of Anthropic's help pages (secondary source): feedback you sent on a chat (5 years), flagged chats' inputs and outputs (up to 2 years), and safety classifier scores (up to 7 years).

ui.platforms: Web (claude.ai and chatgpt.com) is the main path. iOS and Android apps have the same settings but with a different layout. Claude link deletion is confirmed on web.
screens: CLAUDE: open claude.ai. Click your profile/initials button at the bottom-left of the left sidebar, then choose Settings from the menu.

Claude Settings: a left-hand list of tabs that includes Privacy and 'Your Claude'/Memory (the order is not confirmed in any source). In the Privacy tab, the data section has rows with a Manage button on the right: 'Shared chats' and 'Shared artifacts'. Other Privacy items include export data and the 'Help improve our AI models' toggle. The exact order of rows is unverified.

Click Manage next to 'Shared chats'. A modal titled 'Shared chats' lists each chat: its title, date shared, an 'Open chat' link, and a trash/unshare icon. If it's empty, it reads 'No shared content found'.
Click the trash/unshare icon next to a chat. The link is revoked.

Back in Privacy, click Manage next to 'Shared artifacts' for the artifact list. Each artifact has a 'Published'/'Unpublish' control, and the artifact's Share/Published button sits at the top right of the artifact panel.
Claude chat view: the 'Share' button is in the conversation header, top right of an open chat. Its pop-up has a 'Share' button. After sharing, it shows 'Chat shared' with a 'Keep private' option.

Claude memory screen: Settings > Your Claude (or Memory in the older layout) has a toggle ('Memory from chats'/'Generate memory from chats') and a 'Your memory' row with Manage. The memory list shows 'Topics', each of which you can open, edit or delete. Pause and Reset options are on this page.

CHATGPT: click your profile avatar at the bottom-left of the sidebar, then Settings. The Settings modal has a left tab list including Personalization and Data controls (neighbouring tabs elsewhere, e.g. General, Notifications, are not confirmed by these sources).

Data controls tab: a row labelled 'Shared links' with a Manage button on the right (rows like 'Improve the model for everyone' sit nearby). Clicking Manage opens a list of shared chats. Each has a three-dot or trash icon with 'Delete shared link'. A 'More actions' menu holds 'Delete all shared links'.

Personalization tab > Memory: shows 'Memory'/'Enable memory', 'Reference saved memories', 'Reference chat history', and a 'Manage' or 'Memory summary' button. The '•••' menu has 'Delete and turn off memory'. Exact labels depend on your account.
Light or dark default: not verified in any source. The recreation should follow the viewer's device theme and avoid claiming a default.

research.visuals: Best shown as a real screen recording: (1) Claude Settings > Privacy, with the 'Shared chats' and 'Shared artifacts' Manage buttons visible, then the 'Shared chats' modal and the Unshare/trash click. (2) ChatGPT Settings > Data controls > Shared links > Manage, then 'Delete all shared links'. (3) A Claude or ChatGPT memory screen with the toggle switched off. Blur or use demo data in the link lists, because real titles are sensitive. Don't show a live Google search for site:claude.ai/share, as it no longer returns results. The ChatGPT equivalent site:chatgpt.com/share is mentioned in sources, but its current behaviour isn't verified.
research.notes: The topic is real and recent, but the reel's hook needs reframing. In late July 2026, shared Claude chat links were found in Google via site:claude.ai/share. They have since been removed, and only chats people had shared were affected. A safe hook is: 'Anything you've hit Share on is a public link. Check it in 30 seconds.' Avoid implying that private chats leak. Settings labels have changed. Claude's Settings now has 'Your Claude' (older layout: 'Memory'), the Privacy rows read 'Shared chats' and 'Shared artifacts', and Anthropic's own help page also uses 'Data controls'. Artifact sharing changed around September 16, 2026: new shares need a Claude account, and only legacy published artifacts are open to anyone. The exact Claude Share dialog wording (Public/Private visibility versus 'Chat shared' and 'Keep private') comes from third-party pages, so confirm it on a live screen before recreating it. ChatGPT memory labels vary by account, because OpenAI says controls may be missing depending on plan, region or platform. Test in your own accounts before filming. Do not show real chat titles. Unsharing does not delete the chat, and deleting a chat does not delete its memory, so tell viewers to do all three steps (unshare, delete chat, clear memory). ChatGPT's Business plan can't disable sharing, only Enterprise can. The search tool could not retrieve Anthropic's current help-center page for 'Shared artifacts' directly, so the artifact unpublish steps rest on support.claude.com plus third-party guides.
